transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been having a little trouble keeping things in order at work lately. It's probably just me being a bit scattered, but... I work at a dry cleaner, and I just can't seem to keep my station organized anymore. The claim tickets, the receipts, little workshop notes, the customer jobs... they all just sort of get piled together. And then I look at the pile and I just... I don't know what to handle first. 

I feel terrible even bringing it up, because I know everyone gets a little messy sometimes, right? I just hope I'm not wasting your time with this... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
Has this difficulty with keeping things organized been a struggle for you throughout most of your life, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, it's... it's probably been around for a while. I hate to admit it, because I really don't want to sound like I'm just making excuses for myself, you know? But, um... yes, even way back in grade school, I guess it was a bit of a thing. 

My teachers—they were always very kind about it, they told my mother I was a bright girl, which was sweet of them to say! But they did always mention that I was... well, "scattered" was the word they used a lot. I was always accidentally talking out of turn, or losing my school papers, and... they usually had to give me extra reminders to actually finish my work. 

I always just thought I was a bit too chatty, or maybe just not trying hard enough to be a good student. Is that... does that help answer your question? I hope I'm not oversharing or making a big deal out of normal kid stuff.
Do you often feel like you have a constant need to be moving, or do you find it hard to sit still for long periods of time?

Um, well... I suppose I do have a little trouble with that sometimes. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything! I'm sure it's just a bit of restless energy, which is normal, right? 

But, um... like, when I'm at church committee meetings, or when we have those fabric-care trainings at work... I do find myself getting up a lot. I always try to make it useful, you know? Like, I'll get up to grab a glass of water, or fetch some papers, or just go check on something really quick. It's just... I notice that everyone else seems perfectly fine just sitting there the whole time, and I'm the only one popping up and down. 

I try to be quiet about it so I don't bother anyone. I just... my legs get a little antsy if I sit for too long. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before someone has finished asking you a question, or perhaps interrupting others when they are speaking?

Um... oh dear, I suppose I do that a bit, yes. I don't mean to be rude, I really don't! I just... I get so eager to help, I think. 

Like, if my daughter is asking me something, or a customer at the counter, or even the trainer at work... sometimes I just jump right in with an answer before they've even finished their sentence. I think I know what they're going to say, and I just want to be helpful and quick! But... well, sometimes I find out I actually answered the wrong thing because I didn't wait to hear the whole question. 

It's just me trying to be efficient, I think, but I always feel terrible when I realize I've cut someone off. I try so hard to be a good listener. Is that... is that a very bad thing to do? I hope it doesn't make me sound awful.
Looking back at your day-to-day life, would you say that your difficulty with sitting still and your tendency to interrupt others happen almost every single day, or does it come and go in waves?

Um, well... I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it's... it's probably an everyday sort of thing. I really wish I could say it only happens every now and then! But, um... yes, I think the fidgeting and the... the jumping into conversations... it does happen pretty much every day. 

I mean, I always try my best to keep it under control, especially at work or at church. I don't want to be a bother to anyone, you know? But it just feels like my motor is always running, just a little bit, no matter what day of the week it is. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm completely out of control! I really do try very hard to be polite and patient. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

When you look at your struggles overall, do you feel that your difficulty with staying organized and focused is more of a problem for you than the restlessness and the tendency to interrupt others, or are both equally challenging?

Um... oh, that's a hard one to answer. I... I suppose they both cause a bit of trouble, if I'm being perfectly honest. I don't want to make it sound like I'm doing a terrible job everywhere I go, but... well... 

I guess the organizing and focusing part has caused some... little hiccups at the dry cleaners. You know, just minor things! But... well, sometimes an order might get finished a little late, or a bill gets a tiny bit confused. And then, with the interrupting and the restlessness... I think it makes people a bit tense sometimes. A few of the girls at work, and some of the customers... they've seemed a little frustrated with me. I hate making people upset, I really do. 

And, um... at church... I actually stepped back from leading some of the planning committees recently. I just... I could tell people were getting a little annoyed when I couldn't keep the paperwork straight or when I kept jumping into their sentences. I thought it would be better for everyone if I just helped out in the background instead. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds like a lot of problems. I really try to keep everything running smoothly. Do you think... is it normal for both sides of it to be, well, equally difficult like that? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
